_why: The lane map of docs/2026-09-30-parallel-development-design.md §5, as paths a tool can check (MOD9). tools/merge-branch.mjs prints which lanes a branch touched, and never refuses a merge on it: a lane is how the parent dispatches branches that do not share files, and the report tells the parent when one crossed. Each lane's title is the design's own; a test holds the two tables together and holds that every path here still matches a tracked file. `parent` lists the records a subagent never edits. `laneless` lists what belongs to no lane on purpose, each group with its reason; a test refuses a tracked file that is in no lane and not listed there, so a new path is placed when it is added, never left outside silently (LEFT1). Globs: `*` stays inside one folder, `**` crosses folders, `{a,b}` is either, and a path starting `!` carves a narrower lane's files out of a wider one.

lanes.title: Web shell
lanes._why: The page, but its Settings: the frame, the bridge, the atoms, the work frame, every other screen, the modules they share, the catalogues outside Settings' areas, and the page's build and end-to-end suite.

lanes.title: Desktop modules
lanes._why: The modules, the application, and the launcher that starts it (D93), a twin of the modules' taskbar identity (D108). The desktop tree's package versions are the kit the application and the modules run on; the driver has no package of its own.

lanes.title: Tools and records
lanes._why: This repository's own tooling and gates: tools/, the devkit's gates, the gates' declaration and the release workflow that runs them, the desktop suites' Process settings the gates name (MOD8), and the workspace's scripts and ignore rules.

laneless.what: The docs and records: read by every lane and written by the change that makes them stale.
The doctrine and what it is synced into: a canon change re-syncs this repository's own copy and the example family in the same commit, whichever lane asked for it.
The harness's settings for working in this repository.
Build settings every desktop project shares, the driver's and the modules' alike.
